data_notice: Public-sourced claim taken from an already-published URL. Probability is omitted where the original source did not state one word for word; those rows are verdict-only and are not in the Brier set. Link fields marked [U] are unknown and were not invented; those rows are reading-list items and are not scored.
exact_quote: I see a coming productivity boom. I see about a doubling of productivity growth in the coming decade as a result of these technologies.
question: Will US labor productivity growth roughly double, over the decade from 26 Sep 2023, as a result of AI and related technologies, as Brynjolfsson stated?
population: The United States nonfarm business sector (BLS labor productivity)
denominator: Average annual labor-productivity growth in the pre-statement slow-productivity period (2005–2019), as the baseline growth rate being doubled
threshold: About twice that baseline rate, as the average annual growth rate over the decade ending 26 Sep 2033
metric_unit: percent per year (BLS nonfarm business labor productivity, average annual growth)
resolution_rule: Numeric 'about a doubling.' The decade is 26 Sep 2023 to 26 Sep 2033. Baseline is US nonfarm business labor-productivity average annual growth over 2005–2019 (the pre-pandemic slow-productivity period Brynjolfsson has used as the reference; frozen here at 1.4% per year as a representative published figure for that period — if BLS-vintage 2005–2019 growth at resolution rounds to a different figure, double *that* vintage baseline instead, and keep the same 'about' band). KEPT if average annual growth over the 2023–2033 decade is within 0.3 percentage points of twice the baseline ('about a doubling'; frozen band). With a 1.4% baseline that is 2.5–3.1%. BROKEN if the decade average is outside that band. Use BLS nonfarm business labor productivity (the standard quarterly series; annualized average over the window). BLS revisions after the deadline: use the first full vintage published after 26 Sep 2033 covering the window. UNRESOLVABLE only if that BLS series is discontinued with no official successor. Attribution 'as a result of these technologies' is not separately tested: the claim is resolved on the observed growth rate, which is what he said he sees.
resolution_source: US BLS nonfarm business sector labor productivity (quarterly, official series), average annual growth over 26 Sep 2023–26 Sep 2033, first post-deadline vintage.
probability_note: No numerical probability was stated word for word by the original source; the claim is not in the Brier set.
basis: First-person statement in Fortune, 26 Sep 2023. The 'productivity boom' words link to his Brookings 'Machines of Mind' essay; the resolving sentence is the doubling claim. No numerical probability was stated.
base_rate_or_reference_class: US nonfarm labor-productivity growth in the 2005–2019 slow-productivity period (about 1.3–1.5% per year); he has also contrasted this with the 1990s boom.
key_assumptions: The 'coming decade' is the ten years after 26 Sep 2023.
'About a doubling' is resolved with a frozen ±0.3pp band around 2× the 2005–2019 baseline.
BLS nonfarm business labor productivity is the metric (he was speaking about US productivity).
update_triggers: A BLS multi-year run already clearly above or below the doubled band.
A public restatement by Brynjolfsson of the doubling claim or its horizon.
